  "candidates": [
    {
      "startEvent": 234,
      "endEvent": 243,
      "contextStartEvent": 216,
      "contextEndEvent": 246,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "He lives within my heart.",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "unclear",
      "protection": "no",
      "emotionalDevices": ["comfort", "identity"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "Craig endorses the hymn as illustrating experiential knowledge. Whether it replaces justification for identifying an experience as the risen Jesus remains unclear: E229–246 explicitly propose experience as a basic ground, rather than offering the lyric alone as public proof. No objection-neutralizing rule is stated."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 1897,
      "endEvent": 1922,
      "contextStartEvent": 1892,
      "contextEndEvent": 1935,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "eternal salvation, which is an incommensurable good to which the suffering in this world cannot even be compared.",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "no",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": ["comfort"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "Salvation supplies a proposed overriding purpose, but the connection between particular animal suffering and optimal salvation is not established. E1893 and E1919 mark the account as speculation and possibility. The unlimited comparison suggests protection, but this initial use does not yet expressly make every contrary pattern irrelevant."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 1951,
      "endEvent": 1955,
      "contextStartEvent": 1924,
      "contextEndEvent": 1955,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "we're in no position at all to say when we see some instance of evil",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "no",
      "protection": "yes",
      "emotionalDevices": ["none"],
      "confidence": "high",
      "explanation": "The butterfly-effect discussion supplies an argument, so this is not slogan substitution. Its unrestricted conclusion blocks probable judgments against any observed evil by invoking unknown downstream goods. E1940–1951 establish possible consequential complexity, but do not establish that it defeats every probability judgment about God's reasons."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 2006,
      "endEvent": 2019,
      "contextStartEvent": 1965,
      "contextEndEvent": 2019,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "that's a burden of proof the atheist cannot bear.",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "no",
      "protection": "yes",
      "emotionalDevices": ["none"],
      "confidence": "high",
      "explanation": "Craig dismisses alternative provision as unknowable speculation and requires proof that God cannot have sufficient reasons. This insulates the account from the probabilistic challenge using unrestricted possible purposes. E1965–1968 fairly acknowledge his own speculation; the fossil-fuel argument is substantive, although it does not establish the demanded impossibility standard."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 2044,
      "endEvent": 2058,
      "contextStartEvent": 2028,
      "contextEndEvent": 2058,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "We don't know what would happen in such a world.",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "no",
      "protection": "yes",
      "emotionalDevices": ["none"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "After Alex explicitly distinguishes implausibility from impossibility at E2038–2043, Craig again invokes unknowable salvation outcomes to neutralize alternative worlds. His apparent-age example supplies an ordinary reason against one alternative. The protective extension is treating unknown conversion totals as sufficient to block the wider comparative objection."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 2094,
      "endEvent": 2102,
      "contextStartEvent": 2059,
      "contextEndEvent": 2102,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "the atheist seems to know more about divine psychology than I think he really does.",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "no",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": ["none"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "Craig answers the nonsentient-animal alternative by demanding justification that God should choose it and questioning access to divine psychology. This continues the earlier protective pattern, but E2094–2099 can also be a legitimate distinction between possibility and obligation. The sentence does not independently establish that disagreement proves a critic's defect."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 2559,
      "endEvent": 2570,
      "contextStartEvent": 2515,
      "contextEndEvent": 2592,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "And there's no way the atheist could prove such a speculation.",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "no",
      "protection": "yes",
      "emotionalDevices": ["comfort"],
      "confidence": "high",
      "explanation": "Renewing the salvation defense after an audience question, Craig requires proof of a feasible world with a better salvation balance and declares such proof unavailable. Unknown optimal outcomes thereby shield the suffering pattern. Earlier reasoning is explicitly recalled at E2557–2558, making this a protected argument rather than an unsupported slogan."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 2712,
      "endEvent": 2722,
      "contextStartEvent": 2703,
      "contextEndEvent": 2727,
      "speaker": "O",
      "quote": "I don't know. I'm not God, and neither does Alex O'Connor.",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "yes",
      "protection": "yes",
      "emotionalDevices": ["none"],
      "confidence": "high",
      "explanation": "The audience member uses human nondivinity to settle whether suffering can count as evidence at all. No reason establishes that limited knowledge removes its evidential relevance. E2717–2719 cite Craig's positive arguments, but those do not earn the categorical exclusion of suffering announced at E2712–2714."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 2747,
      "endEvent": 2759,
      "contextStartEvent": 2728,
      "contextEndEvent": 2783,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "the problem of evil isn't a problem.",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "unclear",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": ["ridicule"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "The quoted maxim dismisses the problem for believers with good grounds, calling alternative grounds 'lousy.' E2734–2745 supply a conditional inference and earlier arguments supply its proposed premise. Unclear is whether this merely weighs competing evidence or excludes suffering regardless of merits; the maxim does not establish that distinction."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 2834,
      "endEvent": 2842,
      "contextStartEvent": 2810,
      "contextEndEvent": 2845,
      "speaker": "O",
      "quote": "I am not God, and neither are you.",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "yes",
      "protection": "yes",
      "emotionalDevices": ["none"],
      "confidence": "high",
      "explanation": "After Alex asks about comparative expectations, the audience member renews the nondivinity refrain instead of explaining why those expectations cannot be assessed. E2814–2816 expressly reserve God's existence to other criteria. The scope could concern a bare creator, but the response still excludes the evidence rather than addressing the requested comparison."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 2942,
      "endEvent": 2950,
      "contextStartEvent": 2903,
      "contextEndEvent": 2950,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "with an open mind and an open heart",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "no",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": ["comfort"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "Craig answers unequal access by asserting universal spiritual drawing and knowledge available to receptive people. Openness could make nonbelief evidence of a personal defect, but he never explicitly draws that inference. E2938 supplies a biblical rationale; this remains a conditional experiential claim with uncertain protective use, not a compact substitute for argument."
    }
  ],
  "contrasts": [
    {
      "startEvent": 465,
      "endEvent": 494,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "Either full means that it can take no more guests.",
      "explanation": "Alex distinguishes occupancy from inability to admit guests, then gives a finite-hotel comparison. His conclusion that the example is unintuitive rather than contradictory summarizes explicit reasoning, regardless of whether the analogy ultimately succeeds."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 2507,
      "endEvent": 2509,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "that would suggest that Michael Murray's speculation is incorrect.",
      "explanation": "Craig conditionally accepts the force of Alex's reported patient counterexample against the proposed brain explanation. This limits a specific hypothesis in response to contrary evidence, consistent with his earlier acknowledgment that it was speculative at E2481–2482."
    }
  ]
